messages:
ravi: Quick sync 1: I finished the tangelo-13b embedding onboarding sweep. Compared fp16, per-tensor int8 (pt8), per-channel int8 (pc8), asymmetric per-channel int6 (int6-pc-asym), and a hybrid int4-act/int8-wt config. Eval = semantic-suite-multilang-v3 (60k queries). High-level: best latency with int6-pc-asym and hybrid, but quality tradeoffs vary by cohort; summary table below.

meera: Paste the numbers and seeds pls.

ravi: Seeds 11/19/23, median of 3 runs. Short table (recall@1 / recall@5 / p95_ms / id_flip_k5):

```
config                 r@1    r@5    p95_ms   id_flip_k5
tangelo:fp16           0.883  0.946  46ms     0.09%
tangelo:pt8            0.872  0.940  37ms     0.55%
tangelo:pc8            0.881  0.944  38ms     0.15%
int6-pc-asym           0.876  0.942  31ms     0.38%
hybrid-int4            0.878  0.943  29ms     0.27%
```

ravi: Notes: pt8 gives good latency but large id-flip & false-neighbor increases, especially on low-resource languages. pc8 recovers most quality. int6-pc-asym reduces p95 by ~33% vs fp16 but has a small r@1 hit concentrated on short queries and Arabic-like scripts. Hybrid balances latency and tail stability.

zack: Which cohorts are worst? short queries or rare-vocab?

ravi: Cohort breakdown (r@1 fp16 -> int6-pc-asym): short(<7 tokens) 0.812 -> 0.800 (-0.012), cjk (zh/ja/ko) 0.764 -> 0.758 (-0.006), ar 0.732 -> 0.701 (-0.031), head queries 0.915 -> 0.916 (+0.001). So biggest hit on ar and very low-freq tokens.

hana: Did you compute any stability metrics besides id_flip? KSI or knn-consistency?

ravi: Yes - knn-consistency (overlap(top10_fp16, top10_quant)) median: pt8=0.71, pc8=0.88, int6-pc-asym=0.84, hybrid=0.86. Also computed silhouette_k3: fp16 0.431 -> int6 0.399 (loss), pc8 0.424. UMAP diffs uploaded: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/tangelo/4890012345-umap-diff.png

zack: Any layer-level drift insights? Which layers cause the most L2 drift?

ravi: Ran per-layer L2 drift on 10k sampled queries: proj_out layers 13-15 and layernorm 2 in block 12 show the highest mean drift. Targeted clamp on proj_out 13-15 (clamp=0.93) improves short-query recall by ~0.006 and lowers id_flip by ~0.11pp. Command I used: 

```
rbw-quant --model tangelo-13b --mode pc6-asym --idf-calib 4096 --clamp-layers "proj_out:13-15" --calib-samples 8192 --out ./runs/tangelo/pc6_asym_clamp
```

meera: Interesting you used idf-weighted calibration. Did that help per-lang?

ravi: Yes, idf-weighted sampling during calibration reduces bias toward head tokens and helps low-resource languages marginally. Per-lang r@5 for ar improved by ~0.008 vs uniform calib. Still not perfect though.

hana: Ops - can we get a dedicated run to validate the pc6-asym+clamp config at scale? Prefer 3xA100 for 5h to avoid noisy neighbor variance. @ops-bot

ops-bot: Reservation made: dedicated-ml-5, 3x A100, window tomorrow 19:30-00:30 UTC, job-id: rbw-9577. Artifacts path: /artifacts/rbw-9577/4890012345/. :white_check_mark:

zack: Proposed canary gates: if overall r@1 delta <= 0.004, short-query delta <= 0.01, and id_flip_k5 <= 0.30% -> start 7-day 5% canary on staging with alerts on id_flip and per-lang drifts. Otherwise abort. Hana/Meera ok?

hana: OK. Also require silhouette_k3 drop < 0.02 and knn-consistency >= 0.82. Add NN id-flip fuzz test (sample 60k) during canary.

meera: Add human sanity-check: 2k ar queries for manual review of top3 neighbors (label relevance). If human-judged precision drops >1.0pp, abort.

ravi: I'll queue the dedicated run under rbw-9577 using idf-calib 8k and targeted clamp on proj_out 13-15 and post full artifacts (UMAPs, per-layer drift tables, id-flip histograms, knn-consistency bootstraps) to the artifact path. TL;DR: pc8 close to fp16; int6 asym gives latency wins but small tail risks on ar/short queries; targeted clamp + idf-weighted calib mitigate much of the loss. Canary gates proposed. Will report back with final numbers after the dedicated run. :rocket:
